summary: Isotretinoin is an oral retinoid (13-cis-retinoic acid) indicated only for severe recalcitrant nodular acne unresponsive to conventional therapy including systemic antibiotics. It is a potent teratogen (Pregnancy Category X) carrying a boxed warning and is available only through the FDA-mandated iPLEDGE REMS restricted-distribution program. A single 15-20 week course at 0.5-1 mg/kg/day in two divided doses with food produces prolonged remission in many patients. Key toxicities include teratogenicity, psychiatric effects, hypertriglyceridemia, hepatotoxicity, and pseudotumor cerebri.
indications: Severe recalcitrant nodular acne (nodules >=5 mm) in non-pregnant patients unresponsive to conventional therapy including systemic antibiotics

moa: Isotretinoin is 13-cis-retinoic acid, a retinoid related to retinoic acid and retinol (vitamin A). At 0.5-1 mg/kg/day it inhibits sebaceous gland function and keratinization, reducing sebaceous gland size, sebum secretion, and inhibiting sebaceous gland differentiation; the exact mechanism is unknown.

Patients who are or may become pregnant and cannot comply with iPLEDGE requirements
Hypersensitivity to isotretinoin or any component (including soybean/vitamin A sensitivity)

preg: Pregnancy Category X - absolutely contraindicated. Isotretinoin is a potent human teratogen; there is an extremely high risk that life-threatening birth defects will result if pregnancy occurs in any amount, even for short periods. Documented defects include craniofacial (skull, ear, eye, cleft palate, facial dysmorphia), CNS (hydrocephalus, microcephaly, cranial nerve deficit), cardiovascular, thymus, and parathyroid abnormalities, plus IQ scores below 85, spontaneous abortion, and premature birth. Patients who can become pregnant must use two effective forms of contraception (or commit to abstinence) starting 1 month before, throughout, and for 1 month after therapy, with monthly pregnancy testing under iPLEDGE. If pregnancy occurs, discontinue immediately and refer to an OB-GYN experienced in reproductive toxicity.
lact: Not recommended during breastfeeding. Because of its lipophilicity and teratogenic/retinoid activity, isotretinoin may be excreted in human milk and could harm a nursing infant; avoid use while breastfeeding.
renal: No specific FDA-labeled renal dose adjustment is provided. Use with general caution.
hepatic: Clinical hepatitis and mild-to-moderate transaminase elevations (about 15% of patients) have occurred. Obtain baseline and periodic LFTs; if elevations are clinically significant or persist, reduce the dose or discontinue.

major: Tetracyclines (minocycline, doxycycline) - increased risk of pseudotumor cerebri; avoid concurrent use
Vitamin A and supplements containing vitamin A - additive hypervitaminosis A toxicity; avoid
moderate: Systemic corticosteroids - additive risk of bone loss/osteoporosis
Progestin-only ('minipill') contraceptives - may be inadequate; not recommended as a sole method
minor: St. John's wort - may reduce hormonal contraceptive effectiveness
interactions.food: Must be taken with food (ideally a high-fat meal); food more than doubles Cmax and AUC and is required for adequate absorption.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol; it can worsen hypertriglyceridemia and hepatotoxicity.
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor fasting lipids and liver function tests; may elevate triglycerides, cholesterol, transaminases, blood glucose, and CPK, and may lower HDL.

common: Dry skin, dry mouth, dry nose, epistaxis
serious: Depression, psychosis, suicidal ideation and behavior, aggression
Hearing impairment (may be permanent), vision/night-vision impairment, corneal opacities
rare: Severe skin reactions (erythema multiforme, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis)
Premature epiphyseal closure, hyperostosis, decreased bone mineral density
emergency: Life-threatening fetal birth defects if taken during pregnancy - discontinue immediately and seek OB-GYN referral
Suicidal thoughts or behavior / acute psychiatric crisis
Severe abdominal pain, rectal bleeding, or severe diarrhea (pancreatitis or IBD)
Severe headache with visual changes, nausea, and vomiting (pseudotumor cerebri)
Signs of severe allergic/skin reaction or anaphylaxis

monitoring: Pregnancy tests: two negative tests before starting, then monthly during therapy and one after the last dose (iPLEDGE requirement)
Fasting lipid panel at baseline and periodically (weekly/biweekly until response established)
Liver function tests at baseline and periodically
Psychiatric assessment: depression, mood changes, suicidal ideation at each visit
Visual and hearing changes; bone/musculoskeletal symptoms
iPLEDGE: monthly prescriber confirmation, contraception verification, and pharmacist authorization before each 30-day dispense

Complete required monthly pregnancy tests and answer iPLEDGE educational questions before each prescription
Always take capsules with food; taking them without food greatly reduces effectiveness
Report any feelings of sadness, depression, mood changes, or thoughts of self-harm immediately
Avoid vitamin A supplements, tetracycline antibiotics, and alcohol
Do not donate blood during treatment or for 1 month afterward
Avoid cosmetic procedures (waxing, dermabrasion, laser) during and for ~6 months after therapy; use lip balm, moisturizer, and sun protection
Report severe headache, blurred vision, abdominal pain, rectal bleeding, or hearing changes promptly
pk: Clinical acne improvement over weeks; sebum reduction dose/duration related
Tmax ~5.3 hr fed (3.2 hr fasted); food more than doubles Cmax/AUC
Single 15-20 week course often gives prolonged/complete remission
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); protect from light
pearls: Available ONLY through the iPLEDGE REMS - prescriber, pharmacy, and patient must all be enrolled and activated; dispensed in 30-day supplies with a fresh authorization each fill
Pregnancy Category X with a boxed contraindication/warning: 'CAUSES BIRTH DEFECTS - DO NOT GET PREGNANT'; two negative pregnancy tests required before starting and monthly tests during therapy
Absorption depends on food - counsel to always take with a meal (preferably high-fat) to avoid treatment failure
Screen and monitor for depression, suicidal ideation, and mood changes throughout therapy
Hypertriglyceridemia is common (~25% with marked elevations); triglycerides >800 mg/dL can precipitate acute pancreatitis - monitor lipids
Avoid concomitant tetracyclines (pseudotumor cerebri risk) and vitamin A (additive toxicity)
missed: If a dose is missed, skip it and take the next dose at the regular time with food; do not double up. Do not attempt to make up missed doses by taking extra. Maintain the twice-daily schedule and contact the prescriber if multiple doses are missed.
overdose: Isotretinoin overdose produces signs of hypervitaminosis A (headache, vomiting, facial flushing, cheilosis, abdominal pain, dizziness, ataxia); effects are generally transient and reversible. Management is supportive. Because of the teratogenic risk, any overdose in a patient who can become pregnant warrants pregnancy assessment and counseling.
